Subject: BlueHarbor deployment routing — security checkpoints & evidence

Hi Lena / Ravi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the items we agreed and the asks I captured on the call so we can keep momentum: 

- Deployment options under consideration: Hosted API (fastest to prod), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), Private VPC (customer VPC with BAA / on-prem discussion).
- BlueHarbor priority: PHI protection + audit readiness for upcoming vendor review (targeted for late May).
- BlueHarbor asks: 1) list of SOC 2 artifacts we can provide, 2) whether a DLP/ingress filtering layer is supported on hosted, 3) timeline and lead times for Dedicated capacity provisioning, and 4) an initial BAA draft.

Next steps (from Redwood):
1) I will share a short SOC 2 artifact index and an initial BAA draft by EOD Wednesday.
2) Karthik to confirm what infra/network evidence we can include for hosted vs VPC (KV cache handling, separation controls).
3) Grace to propose an evidence-collection timeline aligned to your vendor audit (late May).

Attachments: initial SOC2 summary + BAA draft (changing details into editable BAA).

Can you confirm the audit window (exact dates) and whether procurement will need a signature-ready BAA or a redlineable draft? I want to tailor the deliverable.

Thanks —
Priyom

Priyom —

Appreciate the recap. Vendor audit is scheduled May 22–26 (internal auditors will start the questionnaire week of May 29th). Procurement will want a signature-ready BAA but procurement/legal will also submit redlines. Main technical asks from security: 

- Confirm whether PHI persists on Redwood systems for Hosted API (we need data residency / retention controls).
- SOC 2: we specifically need CC6 (change management), CC7 (logical & physical access), and evidence of vendor incident response timelines.
- If we choose Dedicated capacity, lead time for reserving a pool (we have GPU sizing questions).
- For Private VPC: can we run in our AWS account with customer-managed KMS and do you support cross-account VPC peering?

If you can supply the SOC2 index + BAA draft, we can start internal review. Also please include a short note comparing risk surface of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC in the doc (2–3 bullets each) — that'll help us present to security.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Security & Compliance | BlueHarbor Health

Subject: Re: BlueHarbor deployment routing — security checkpoints & evidence

Quick update —

- SOC2 artifacts: we can provide an index and sample artifacts for CC6 and CC7 (change logs, access onboarding logs, and role matrices). We can also share our SOC2 Type II report under NDA; otherwise we'll provide our SOC2 summary and the artifact index. See attached short index (attached as Redwood_SOC2-Summary.pdf).
- Hosted API: PHI is processed in-memory during inference and cached tokens are covered by retention controls; persistent PHI storage is not typical for hosted unless a customer uploads data to Redwood-managed storage — we will document the retention/ttl controls and deletion processes. Hosted does not support customer-managed KMS or cross-account VPC peering.
- Dedicated capacity: provides stronger isolation (dedicated GPU pool) and we can offer a more aggressive data retention policy; still Redwood-managed infra but with tenant isolation. Lead time for reserving a Dedicated pool: typically 6–8 weeks for guaranteed capacity; we can often accelerate to 3–4 weeks if a partial pool is sufficient.
- Private VPC: we support deployment into a customer VPC in AWS with cross-account peering and customer-managed KMS — this is the recommended option if BlueHarbor needs KMS control and maximum separation. On-prem deployments are possible but require an engineering engagement (longer lead time).

I will drop the SOC2 index and short Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC risk bullets into the Drive folder and share the docusign BAA link once Monica confirms the template.

-Karthik

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-Summary.pdf (artifact index)
